samples.summary: Read walk recurses into nested tables; the write (`Doc.applyInlineStyle`) does not — reintroducing the #715 "can only add, never remove" trap for selections spanning a table that contains a nested table
samples.evidence: `visitTable` (range-runs.ts:68-83) recurses: `if (cellBlock.type === 'table' && cellBlock.tableData) visitTable(cellBlock)`. The write it claims to mirror does not: `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:415-429) iterates `cell.blocks` and calls `store.applyStyle(cellBlock.id, 0, len)` only when `len = getBlockTextLength(cellBlock) > 0`; a nested table block has `inlines: []` so `len === 0` and its inner cell blocks are never styled. Consequence: for a cross-block selection covering a table whose nested table content differs (e.g. outer runs bold, nested runs not), the read reports `allOn === false` / `'mixed'` forever, so both `isStyleOnInSelection` (text-editor.ts:3007) and the toolbar's `isStyleOn` always resolve to "apply", the write never touches the nested runs, and the style can never be removed — exactly the failure mode this change set out to fix. The `tableCellRange` branch (range-runs.ts:98) is consistent with the write because it uses `visitWholeBlock` (0 runs for a table block); only `visitTable` diverges.

samples.summary: Collapsed-caret keyboard toggle still reads the RAW run style (no named-style defaults), so Cmd+I in a heading whose named style supplies italic remains a permanent visual no-op and disagrees with the toolbar
samples.evidence: `toggleStyle` falls back to `!!visual[key]` when `isStyleOnInSelection` returns `undefined`, which is exactly the collapsed-caret case. `visual` comes from `getStyleAtCursor()` (text-editor.ts:2974-2988), which returns `{...inline.style}` only — no `resolveStyleInline` defaults. So with a caret inside a Heading 6 (built-in style sets italic) Cmd+I computes `!false` → writes pending `italic: true`, a no-op the user can never undo from the keyboard. The docs toolbar in the same situation reads `getRangeStyleSummary()`, whose collapsed path DOES layer defaults (editor.ts:2787-2803, 2812) and therefore writes `italic: false`. The keyboard/toolbar disagreement the change claims to end still exists for collapsed carets.

samples.summary: The text-box (slides) `getRangeStyleSummary` was not migrated to the shared walk and omits named-style inline defaults, so in text-boxes the toolbar and the now-defaults-aware keyboard path disagree
samples.evidence: `text-box-editor.ts:1067-1088` keeps its own `visitInlinesInBlock` that reads `inline.style` raw (`const raw = (inline.style as Record<string, unknown>)[key]`), with no `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), ...)` layer. The shared keyboard path used by the same editor (`TextEditor.toggleStyle` → `isStyleOnInSelection` → `visitStyledRunsInRange`) now DOES layer those defaults. For a heading block inside a docs/slides text-box, Cmd+I writes `italic: false` while the toolbar's `isStyleOn(summary.italic)` sees `undefined` and writes `italic: true` — the two surfaces now invert opposite values on the same selection.

samples.summary: Same-block branch has no `from < to` guard, so a zero-width range reports the run containing the caret instead of no runs — violating the function's documented "runs the range covers" contract
samples.evidence: `if (range.anchor.blockId === range.focus.blockId) { ... visitBlockSlice(id, min, max) }` with min === max reaches `visitBlockSlice`, whose overlap test `inlineEnd > from && pos < to` is true for the inline that strictly contains the offset, so one run is visited for an empty range. Every other branch guards with `if (start < end)` (lines 139, 171), and the code this replaced guarded the linear path the same way. Both current callers happen to pre-check `selection.hasSelection()` (which excludes collapsed same-block ranges, selection.ts:668-675), so nothing misbehaves today, but the exported helper silently reports style for an empty range for any future caller — and `isStyleOnInSelection` would then return a verdict from a run the write would not touch.

samples.summary: The slim header/footer B/I/U Toggles have no `pressed` prop, so their visual state is uncontrolled local state and does not follow the range summary the click handlers now read
samples.evidence: `<Toggle size="sm" onPressedChange={toggleBold} ... aria-label="Bold">` (and the Italic/Underline twins at 458/467) pass no `pressed`, unlike the shared `TextFormatGroup` which was updated to `pressed={isStyleOn(styleSummary?.bold)}`. The handler now decides add-vs-remove from `getRangeStyleSummary()`, but the button keeps flipping its own internal pressed state, so the indicator can show "bold on" while the range is unbolded (and vice-versa) — the same read/display divergence the change fixes elsewhere. The `summary` state already fetched at line 309/318 is available for this.

verdict.reason: The claimed asymmetry exists exactly as described. range-runs.ts:68-83 (`visitTable`) recurses into nested table blocks (`if (cellBlock.type === 'table' && cellBlock.tableData) visitTable(cellBlock)`), and this branch is reached for tables inside a top-level cross-block selection (range-runs.ts:164-166). The mirrored write, Doc.applyInlineStyle document.ts:415-428, iterates only `cell.blocks` and styles a cell block only when `getBlockTextLength(cellBlock) > 0`; since table blocks are built with `inlines: []` (types.ts:528-534) and getBlockTextLength sums inlines (types.ts:326-328), a nested table block yields len 0 and its inner cell blocks are never styled — there is no recursion in the write. Both read consumers use the recursing walk (text-editor.ts:3007-3018 isStyleOnInSelection, used by toggleStyle at text-editor.ts:2895-2898; toolbar at editor.ts:2849) while the write path is doc.applyInlineStyle (text-editor.ts:2921), so a selection spanning a table with differently-styled nested-table runs reads 'mixed'/allOn=false permanently and the toggle always resolves to 'apply' — the style can be added but never removed. Nested tables are reachable in practice via Doc.insertTableInCell (document.ts:592-602, called from editor.ts:3422), so this is not an unreachable code path. No guard elsewhere prevents nested tables inside a cross-block selection. Real logic bug in the correctness lane (wrong condition / broken read-write invariant), severity major.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. text-editor.ts:2895-2898 falls back to `!!visual[key]` whenever `isStyleOnInSelection` returns undefined, which per text-editor.ts:3007-3009 is precisely the collapsed-caret case. `visual` derives from `getStyleAtCursor()` (text-editor.ts:2974-2988), which returns only `{...inline.style}` with no `resolveStyleInline`/`styleDefaultsForBlock` layer, and named-style inline defaults are never materialized into runs (only block spacing is, named-styles.ts:150-166). BUILTIN_STYLES 'heading-6' sets `italic: true` (named-styles.ts:91) and blockStyleId maps heading level 6 to it (named-styles.ts:105-110), so a caret in a Heading 6 has a raw run style without italic: Cmd+I (wired at text-editor.ts:876-881) computes `!false` and stores pending `italic: true`, a visual no-op. The toolbar in the same state layers defaults (editor.ts:2787-2803, 2811-2817) and writes `italic: false` (text-format-group.tsx:103-107 with style-summary.ts:19-21), so the keyboard/toolbar divergence is real on a reachable path. The only inaccuracy is "never undo" — because `visual` merges pending (text-editor.ts:2886-2888), a second press does write italic:false — which reduces impact but does not refute the wrong-fallback logic bug.

finding.summary: Header/footer B/I/U can no longer turn a style OFF for selections inside header/footer table cells (empty range summary)
finding.evidence: The slim header/footer toggles now decide from `editor.getRangeStyleSummary()`. That implementation (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2891-2945) resolves cell-internal blocks through `layout.blockParentMap` — the BODY layout only (declared at editor.ts:937; header/footer cell parentage lives in `headerLayout`/`footerLayout` and is merged only into `doc.setBlockParentMap` at editor.ts:1405-1412). For a header/footer selection whose endpoints are cell-internal blocks, `doc.getBlockIndex(...)` returns -1 (context blocks are the header's top-level blocks), `layout.blockParentMap.get(...)` returns undefined, and the last fallback only covers `anchor.blockId === focus.blockId`. So any multi-block-within-one-cell or cross-cell selection in a header/footer table produces `{}` → `isStyleOn(undefined) === false` → the click always sends `{bold:true}`, and bold can never be removed. The previous `getSelectionStyle()` used `doc.findBlock`, which resolves header/footer + cell blocks, so it did toggle correctly. Note the keyboard path added in this diff uses `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap` (text-editor.ts:3998-4002) and is correct here, so keyboard and toolbar now disagree — the opposite of the change's stated goal.

verdict.reason: The described implementation is not in the tree. `getRangeStyleSummary` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2774-2876) makes no `layout.blockParentMap` lookup at all; its range branch delegates to `visitStyledRunsInRange(doc, range, ...)` at editor.ts:2849 (the only `layout.blockParentMap` mention nearby is a comment at editor.ts:2843 describing the OLD lookup that was replaced). That shared walk (packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:112-142) resolves cell parentage via `doc.blockParentMap` — explicitly the merged body+header+footer map, populated at editor.ts:1406-1413 from headerLayout/footerLayout — and handles multi-block-within-one-cell by slicing each cell block. Cross-cell selections fall through range-runs.ts:144-172, which normalizes endpoints to the parent table id and indexes `doc.getContextBlocks()`, which is header/footer-aware (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:97-101), then walks the table whole via `visitTable`. So the claimed `{}` summary does not occur. The claimed keyboard/toolbar divergence is also absent: `TextEditor.isStyleOnInSelection` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3007-3019) calls the same `visitStyledRunsInRange`, not `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap`. Regression tests pin the exact scenario: packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:355-397 asserts a two-block header-cell selection (forward and backward) reports `bold === true` and that Cmd+B clears bold on both blocks.
